title: The coefficient-free twisted-path description of the Weil group
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], geometric Frobenius $\gamma:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $X_0$ be geometrically connected, separated and of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose a geometric point $b$ of $X$. Write $F_a$ for the finite-etale fibre functor at a geometric point $a$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. A path $a\rightsquigarrow a'$ is a natural isomorphism $F_a\to F_{a'}$.

The set of pairs $(n,p)$, where $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $p:b\rightsquigarrow g^n b$, is a group with multiplication
$$(n,p)(m,q)=(n+m,g^m(p)\circ q).$$
Here $g^m(p)$ is the path obtained by applying $p$ to the pullbacks $(g^m)^*P$ of finite etale covers $P$. There is a degree-preserving group isomorphism from these pairs to $W(X_0,b)$ of [def-wf-weil-group], identifying $(0,p)$ with the geometric fundamental-group element $p$. On a finite etale $X_0$-cover $P_0$, the arithmetic action of $(n,p)$ is $p_{P_0\times_{k_0}k}$ followed by the canonical identification of the fibres at $g^n b$ and $b$ over the same geometric point of $X_0$. This characterizes the isomorphism.

Let $x$ be a closed point of $X_0$ with residue field $\kappa(x)$ of degree $e$ over $k_0$, choose a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$, and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be its lift. Since $g^e a=a\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$, reparametrization of lifted points defines a path
$$c_{a,e}:a\rightsquigarrow g^e a,\qquad z\longmapsto z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$$
on every finite etale cover. For every path $\tau:a\rightsquigarrow b$, the pair
$$(e,g^e(\tau)\circ c_{a,e}\circ\tau^{-1})$$
corresponds to the image of geometric Frobenius of $\kappa(x)$ under the decomposition-group map $\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x))\to\pi_1(X_0,b)$ defined by $\tau$. Its degree is $e$. This statement concerns finite etale covers and paths only; it asserts no comparison of sheaf Frobenius operators.
